title: Fix a rocking deck board: pop it out, take out the pebble under it, and lay it back flat
instruction: The middle deck board rocks because a pebble is stuck under it. Take the board out, put the pebble in the black bucket, and lay the board back flat in its slot.
context: Deck boards, floorboards and paving stones start to rock when grit gets under them. They sit in their rows with almost no gap, so there is nothing to take hold of; the way to lift one is to press down on its high end so it pivots on the grit and the other end rises, then take that end with the other hand. Two hands are needed: the board drops back the moment the pressing hand lets go.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A section of decking: three boards, 7 cm front to back x 25 cm side to side x 2.5 cm thick, side by side in a fixed frame of dark wood end strips (1 cm thick, 2.5 cm tall) 0.7 cm beyond both ends. The front and back boards (light wood, fixed) are centred 18.3 and 33.7 cm forward on the centre line. The middle board (darker wood, 150 g, loose) lies in the 8.4 cm wide slot between them, centred 26 cm forward when flat, on a grey pebble 2 x 2 cm and 8 mm thick, 4.5 cm from its left end: its left end stands about 1 cm proud of the other boards, its right end rests on the slot floor. A black bucket (walls 1 cm thick, 3 cm tall, round a 7 x 7 cm floor) stands 15 cm forward and 27 cm left. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler. 1.0: the middle board lies flat in its slot, flush with the boards beside it (no part of it more than 3 mm above their tops, its bottom within 3 mm of the slot floor, its centre within 1 cm of the slot's centre), and the pebble lies in the bucket, everything still for 2 s. 0.5: the pebble lies in the bucket but the board is not lying flush in its slot. 0.0: anything else, including the pebble still in the slot.
reset_notes: Put the pebble back under the middle board, 4.5 cm from its left end, and lay the board on it.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the boards and the pebble are rigid blocks, the outer boards and the frame are fixed in place, and the slot floor is the table top. Loose objects get rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
